title: Runtime compiler constraints index and onboard checks for specialized attention (MoE/GQA/MHA)
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: When onboarding models that use mixture-of-experts (MoE), grouped-query attention (GQA), or multi-headed attention (MHA) variants we frequently hit silent correctness/latency regressions due to incompatible compile flags, missing kernel variant fallbacks, or micro-batching heuristics that differ by architecture. Current model-onboarder collects perf traces but lacks a machine-readable constraints artifact and preflight checks that guarantee a published performance profile will be reproducible across target hardware.

Goal: Implement a "compiler constraints index" (CCI) — a JSON-like artifact produced during onboarding that enumerates required compiler flags, kernel feature gates, per-architecture fallback rules, and minimal test vectors. Integrate CCI into the model-onboarder CI so every model-version publishes a CCI alongside the performance profile and an automated set of acceptance checks that must pass before pinning a kernel profile for runtime rollout.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- CCI schema defined and documented (human-readable + machine-parsable).
- Onboarder CI step that runs a minimal compile-and-smoke-suite across our hardware matrix and emits CCI.
- Automated checks fail model pin publish if CCI checks don't pass (mismatched flags, missing kernels, or failing numeric regressions beyond thresholds).
- Runtime reads CCI at model load to enforce compatible kernel selection and to enable automatic safe fallback policies (e.g., prefer quantized kernel X on A100 if CCI indicates 'quantize_ok' else block).
- Console displays CCI summary on model version page and surfaces incompatibility reasons in rollout UI.

Design notes / constraints:
- Keep CCI minimal: a set of key/value constraints (strings) and named test signatures rather than attempting to encode full compile graph.
- For MoE, include routing invariants (expert count, capacity factor expectations) and per-expert memory footprint hints so runtime can choose tiled vs fused kernels.
- For GQA, capture grouped-head mapping and preferred head-splitting kernel tag.
- For MHA variants, record supported sequence length patterns and KV-cache chunking guidance.

Trade-offs discussed:
- Option A: Bake more logic into CCI so runtime becomes smarter (longer onboarding effort, smaller runtime decisions).
- Option B: Keep CCI strict and minimal, let runtime use conservative fallbacks. We chose Option B for faster rollout and clearer auditability.

Integration points: model-onboarder CI, runtime kernel-selection layer, console model version page, and publish flow that creates/updates pinned kernel profiles.

Success metrics: reduction in post-deploy fallback events by 60% for MoE models, zero silent numerical mismatch incidents for pinned profiles within 90 days, and faster pin onboarding (mean time from push to pinned profile < 48h).
comments: 2025-02-17 — Scoping meeting: aligned with Research (Sofia Nguyen) on MoE routing invariants and with Compiler team (Jamal Ortiz) on feasible minimal flags set. Decided to prototype CCI schema before full CI integration.

2025-02-21 — Prototype CCI schema v0 posted: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/INF/Compiler+Constraints+Index+v0 (design feedback requested). Main open question: how to represent 'soft' vs 'hard' constraints. Recommended pattern: constraint.level = {required|recommended}.

2025-02-26 — Eng sync: chose minimal set of required keys: compiler_flags, kernel_tags, fallback_policy, test_signatures, memory_hints. Added optional fields for quantization_profile and routing_invariants for MoE.

2025-03-01 — CI work started (WIP): added compile matrix job to onboarder CI that runs basic builds for aarch64, x86_64, and NVIDIA A100/RTX8000. Branch: https://github.com/redwood/inference/compare/feature/cci-onboarder. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/3124

2025-03-03 — Early benchmark results from CI smoke suite: MoE-small model compiled with conservative flags shows 4% slower decode compared to unpinned experimental kernel but eliminated a rare 2% token mismatch on edge cases. Decision logged: prefer correctness over marginal perf in initial rollout.

2025-03-04 — Next steps: add runtime read path for CCI (runtime change request ENG-25670), wire Console to surface CCI (PM: Sofia), and author a release note explaining pinning semantics for customers. Also schedule end-to-end test run across Dedicated clusters on 2025-03-10.
